requirements.requirement: Independent recomputation of the decisive quantity (exact m = 2 subgroup coverage)
requirements.evidence: Own Python implementation, sharing no engine code. It builds the k = 20 curve from p = 1048573 and A = 926 (short Weierstrass; #E = 1049624 = 8r is verified by a Legendre point count; s = A/3 = 349833 = pkm_t0_shift; d = 3s^2 + a = 1). It builds the t0-bits base (roots z of z^2 - wz + d, x = z + s, both signs) and the bits base (x in [lo, lo + 2^t)), forms all ordered pair sums, and tests [r]S = O. All 3000 census rows reproduce exactly in columns, base_points, covered_points, covered_points_all_cosets and coverage_exact. A direct [r]S test on every distinct sum reproduces t0-bits L* (82, 212, 424), lo = 0 (4, 36, 148), all 5 P0a anchors, bits lo = 0 (12, 42, 162), bits@797820 t4 = 78 (11 columns), bits@976503 t5 = 198 (24), bits@908172 t6 = 536 (42) and bits@233902 t5 = 184. Every t0 base is closed under T0 and negation. Isogeny-base coverage (64, 214, 34, 80, 528) was not recomputed independently. It agrees with the engine replay and with the prior iso-census (curve25519_isogeny_seed_20261103/data/k20.jsonl), and its counting code (decomposable_points + subgroup filter) is the code validated here on the t0 and bits bases.

requirements.requirement: Failed predictions reported as failed; nothing retuned
requirements.evidence: P4 and P4b are reported as failed in the Answer and the predictions table. The rule, bands, lo list, seeds and arms are unchanged from the freeze. The post-data items (columns proxy, covered-per-column selection, census-mismatch note) are labelled exploratory. analysis/analyze.py is disclosed as a post-hoc decision script.

Every claim is a component claim at k = 20, m = 2, mode full, t in {4, 5, 6}, G in {0, 3, 4}, one target seed per t. There is no leaderboard or benchmarks/ row. The rho gap is given as distance remaining ('Rho remains ahead'), not as a gate. The P4-direction result ('beats the best known bits@L per relation') is labelled per-relation only. It notes that the frames come from unmatched censuses and that t0-bits@L* needs more columns (1.56x and 1.09x worse on a columns x per-rel proxy, labelled exploratory). Note: 'all 4 primary cells' are two exact coverage ratios (82/78 and 198/212), each read at G = 0 and G = 3, not four independent observations; the README gives both values.

T7 claims no discrete-log solve, factor-base relation or closure. Per-relation costs are derived (mul-adds per target / coverage_exact), and coverage_exact was recomputed independently (R5). The 6 random-target hits and the planted completeness counts (P8) are checked only by the harness re-summing the returned base points (curve.add, outside F4) and by replay determinism. The relations are not emitted, so they cannot be re-verified independently. No claim rests on them.

errata.text: In run.sh, `echo "end $(date -u +%FT%TZ) rc=$?"` expands $? after the command substitution, so the recorded rc is date's exit status, not the binary's (checked in bash: `false; echo "$(date) rc=$?"` prints rc=0). The README's '28/28 cells with rc=0 in .status' is therefore not evidence of the engine's exit code. Effect on results: none. The validator's replay recorded the binary's own rc = 0 in 28/28 cells with identical outputs. Fix the logger in future scripts; frozen evidence is not rewritten.

'Load average at cell starts was 6.3 to 7.9': the 28 .status start lines show 5.84 to 7.91 (t0lo0_t4_g0 and t0sel_t4_g0 start at 5.84). 6.26 is the first 'cell done' line in run.log. Counts are deterministic, so no result is affected.

'P3 held, so the per-relation ratio is exactly that coverage ratio (78/82 = 0.9512; 198/212 = 0.9340)'. The measured P4 ratios are 0.951218, 0.951220, 0.933952 and 0.933961, against 78/82 = 0.951220 and 198/212 = 0.933962. They agree to at most 1.1e-5 relative because the mul-adds/target ratios are 0.9999893-1.0000000, so 'exactly' should read 'to within 1.1e-5'.

The unpriced native counters of each arm are not listed: pkm_system_fp_mults_uncharged, pkm_grid_fp_mults_uncharged, pkm_t0_target_fp_mults_uncharged, pkm_t0_target_inversions, pkm_t0_base_map_fp_mults_uncharged and pkm_t0_base_inversions. Validator band check (0, 0.1 and 1 per native op): every verdict and the cheapest arm in every cell are unchanged, so the conclusions stand. The listing should be added where the rankings are cited.

'The generic index-calculus baseline is 7.8x rho there (curve25519_algebraic_ecbench_20261102)'. That study's own session measures proj-a at 7.04 / 7.06 / 7.17x rho-neg (w = 0 / 0.1 / 1). It quotes 7.8-7.9x for an earlier 48-run baseline. Cite the range or name the earlier source. The 18x / 9.6e5x / 5.9e6x figures match that README (18.2 / 9.55e5 / 5.85e6). The 547-936 rho group-op range comes from the frame-search README and was not re-derived here.

notes: isogeny@595 (frozen T7 arm, t = 4) is one of five seeds with J = covered = 64 in curve25519_isogeny_seed_20261103/data/k20.jsonl: 595 (15 columns), 700 (13), 885 (11), 1162 (14) and 1907 (13). That study's analyse.py breaks ties toward more columns (key -columns). PROTOCOL.md's paraphrase 'then columns' is ambiguous, and T7's own t0 rule breaks ties toward fewer columns. T7 used the published selection as frozen, so this is not a T7 erratum. P5 and P7 are per-relation verdicts at equal coverage 64 and do not depend on the choice.

The selection search pricing (frozen) counts 2^t quotient square roots per lo. It does not count the square root of rhs(x) per abscissa, up to 2^(t+1) per lo. Adding it would only raise the reported 2.1e6-2.9e7 search cost, so the README's 'Rho remains ahead' direction is unaffected.
